topic.title: Analog Neural Hardware and Physical Learning Dynamics
topic.overview: This topic connects neural computation with circuits and physical dynamical systems. Early papers implement neural operations and gradient-based learning in analog VLSI, where signal representation and circuit behavior shape the algorithm. Later work addresses analog in-memory training, automated circuit design, and the efficiency of digitally simulating physically inspired learning rules.
topic.whyItMatters: An algorithm's cost depends on the substrate that executes it. Operations natural for analog hardware may be expensive to simulate digitally, while device imperfections can invalidate assumptions made by an idealized learning rule.
topic.evolution: The representatives span bit-serial networks and pulse-stream CMOS chips through circuit-level gradient methods. Recent work studies nonideal references in analog training and agent-assisted circuit sizing. Error-based predictive coding takes a complementary route by reformulating the dynamics for digital efficiency, trading direct analog implementability for faster numerical computation.
openQuestions: Which learning rules remain stable under realistic device variation?
How should comparisons account for simulation overhead, physical precision, and end-to-end training energy?
